basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 23.' and it opens 'Vers. 23. Ejecit eum de paradiso. Actus ipse est, et est defectiva locutio irato vel'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 23. Ejecit eum de paradiso. Actus ipse est, et est defectiva locutio irato vel perturbato conveniens, non quod in Deum ullus irae vel perturbationis motus cadat qui est summae tranquillitatis, sed more sacrae Scripturae hoc dictum est, quae de Deo loquens quae sunt hominum ipsi Deo attribuit. Sumat de ligno vitae et vivat. Sicut jam diximus, impleto numero electorum gustaturi erant omnes de ligno vitae, et ad illum statum beatum migraturi. Et, quia se indignum fecerat illo statu, recte custodia ei adhibita | est, ne posset ulterius lignum vitae contingere.
